question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨-\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3},2t-1⟩,$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨-1,-1⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{t}^{2},2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $⟨-1,-1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨-2{t}^{2},2⟩ & =0 \\ (-1)(-2{t}^{2})+(-1)(2) & =0 \\ 2{t}^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 2(t+1)(t-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $t=\pm 1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨-\frac{2(-1)^{3}}{3},2(-1)-1⟩=⟨\frac{2}{3},-3⟩, \\ r(1) & =⟨-\frac{2(1)^{3}}{3},2(1)-1⟩=⟨-\frac{2}{3},1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨-1,-1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the points $(-\frac{2}{3},1)$ and $(\frac{2}{3},-3).$
